手持樂器，以敲擊方式發聲。手持樂器本體，透過敲擊、搖晃、刮奏或撥彈等方式使樂器本: A hand-held instrument, sounded by striking. Hold the body of the instrument and set it vibrating by striking, shaking, scraping or plucking it. In practice, first check that you are holding it correctly, and work on rhythm patterns and melody only once the basic way of sounding it is secure. 拍板作為打擊樂器，其起源可追溯至東亞地區，特別是中國、日本和韓國等文化圈。最早的: The clapper as a percussion instrument can be traced back to East Asia, especially the culture areas of China, Japan and Korea. The earliest clappers appeared in ancient China, first as a tool for keeping time in storytelling, opera and other folk performing arts. Bamboo clappers spread widely in China because the material was easy to come by and the sound is crisp. As cultures across Asia met, clappers took on regional characters: Japan developed the tanban clapper for traditional music, and Korea created a clapper form of its own. In modern society their use has kept widening, from traditional performance into sport and entertainment. The inflatable plastic clapper shows this development plainly, carrying the instrument out of professional music and into popular culture. Today the clapper is a percussion instrument found in cultures around the world, bearing the character of local traditional arts while going on changing with the needs of the time.
拍板音色明亮尖銳，具有清脆的撞擊感。敲擊時產生的聲音直接而乾淨，缺乏複雜的泛音共: The clapper's timbre is bright and sharp, with a crisp impact. The sound is direct and clean, without complex overtone resonance. Its range is fairly narrow, mostly in the middle and upper frequencies, and the timbre is easy to pick out. As an idiophone the clapper resonates through the vibration of the wood itself, and the material changes the warmth of the tone: bamboo clappers sound lighter, wooden ones heavier and fuller. Beside cymbals the clapper is shorter and more forceful, without the ring of metal; beside a xylophone it is plainer and more direct, with no range of pitches. Clappers are often used to mark the strong beats; their sharp tone cuts through a band and brings out the pulse and the liveliness.

樂鞭屬體鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs編號111.12，由兩塊木板以鉸: The slapstick is an idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 111.12, made of two boards joined by a hinge that clap together quickly to make a sound like a whip crack. Sources mention it in modern orchestras, bands and percussion ensembles, and in the percussion section of Western symphony orchestras; in classical scores it may be marked with the French, German or Italian term for "whip" or "wooden clapper", telling the percussionist to make a short, sharp rhythmic effect at a given passage.
樂鞭（slapstick）是拍板類體鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs 編: The slapstick is an idiophone of the clapper kind, Hornbostel–Sachs 111.12, found in European and cross-cultural theatre and used by percussionists in modern orchestras, bands and percussion ensembles. It is built from two wooden boards hinged at one end; clapped together quickly they give a short sound like a whip cracking. There are two forms: in one, each board has a handle and the two are held in both hands and struck together; in the other, one board is longer and one shorter, with a single handle.

The slapstick is an idiophone of the clapper kind, Hornbostel–Sachs 111.12, found in European and cross-cultural theatre and used by percussionists in modern orchestras, bands and percussion ensembles. It is built from two wooden boards hinged at one end; clapped together quickly they give a short sound like a whip cracking. There are two forms: in one, each board has a handle and the two are held in both hands and struck together; in the other, one board is longer and one shorter, with a single handle and a spring hinge, playable with one hand but not as loud as the two-handed type.
樂鞭（slapstick）為體鳴樂器，來源記載其發聲體由兩片木板構成，以一端鉸鏈: The slapstick is an idiophone. Sources describe its sounding body as two wooden boards joined by a hinge at one end; another type has two boards of different length joined by a spring hinge and can be worked with one hand. Clappers in the broad sense are commonly of wood, and some are of metal or ivory, but for the slapstick the sources clearly support wood, a hinge and a spring hinge; the materials of the other parts are not stated.
